meta.colour_note: colour_srgb = mean sRGB (0-255) of a PyMuPDF render of the PDF at 2 px/mm, region eroded 2 mm; vector_fill_srgb = the design fill. A printed mat under real light will differ.

identity.method: Design §3.1 6 / §3.2: a point pair 1.5 mm either side of an edge of each region drawn by a rectangle (its middle first, then 1 mm steps along it, at least 3 mm from its ends; an edge on the mat's own border has no outside), each point where the topmost paint is a flat fill (the 2 px/mm render's 3 x 3 patch: standard deviation under 3/255 in every channel, in sRGB and in a DeviceCMYK render; that CMYK within 2/255 of a fill the content stream states), the inside the region's own fill, the outside another. A probe side passes when its colour is nearer its expected palette colour than half the distance from that colour to the nearest colour of another class (sRGB 0..255, Euclidean), and its nearest palette colour is of its own class; a pair's two sides are of different classes. Stated fills closer than merge_srgb under either conversion are one class (one colour to the eye). Checked here under MuPDF's ICC conversion (the file's SWOP v2 output intent; MuPDF renders the probes) and pdf.js's DeviceCMYK formula - the pdf.js side is formula-only: MuPDF's DeviceCMYK render of each probe put through pdf.js's formula, which shows the palette is separable under it, not that pdf.js renders the mat so. That proof is W1b's loader test on the real mat (design §8, run whenever the mat is present), under pdf.js with its ICC path off (no wasm, no iccUrl: §3.2).
identity.pdfjs_formula: pdf.js src/core/colorspace.js DeviceCmykCS #toRgb (verified against pdfjs-dist 6.4.299 build/pdf.worker.mjs); trace_mat.py pdfjs_cmyk_to_rgb()
